details.label: Summary
details.text: Severe wind and hail (some significant) remains a concern for a few more hours with an ongoing mature supercell

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A relatively long-lived supercell continues to track south-southwest, with a history of 2+ inch diameter hail and 75+ mph measured gusts. Furthermore, MRMS MESH also indicates hail over 2 inches in diameter may be falling with this storm. This supercell is likely benefiting from locally higher buoyancy (i.e. 2000 J/kg MLCAPE) and 50+ kts of effective bulk shear. Nonetheless, MLCINH will continue to increase through the evening, likely resulting in a gradual weakening with time. Until this occurs though, a localized severe threat should persist

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...UP TO 90 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.50-2.50 IN
